title: A Herculaneum scroll read end to end without opening
summary: Machine-learning ink detection on synchrotron scans let papyrologists read about 22 columns of a likely Stoic ethics text from scroll PHerc. 1667. The text is fragmentary because only the inner core survives, and humans transcribed and reviewed every reading.
ai_technology: Machine-learning ink detection with virtual unwrapping

evidence.tested: Readings checked against explicit coverage and papyrological-review criteria; ink recovery validated independently on another scroll (PHerc. Paris 4).
evidence.unknown: The text is fragmentary because only the inner core survives; systematic recovery across the library is described as future work.
evidence.ai_role: Machine learning used for ink detection on synchrotron scans, alongside improved computational unrolling.
